chapter.qtcraft.basics.first.text:
- Break a few logs of a tree with your hand (hold the left mouse button).
- Open the inventory ({key1.inventory}) and turn the logs into planks, then planks into sticks and a crafting table.
- Place the crafting table and use it (right mouse button) to make a wooden pickaxe.
- Mine stone for a stone pickaxe and look for coal: coal and a stick make torches.
- Build a shelter before the night; a day lasts {day.length} s.
chapter.qtcraft.basics.first.title: The first day
chapter.qtcraft.basics.goal.text: QtCraft is a world of blocks. Collect them, build with them, craft tools, smelt ores and stay alive: creatures come out at night and hunger grows while you work.
chapter.qtcraft.basics.goal.title: What to do
chapter.qtcraft.basics.handbook.text: Press {key.handbook} at any time. Every block, item, creature and biome has a page with its values, its recipes and links to where it comes from and what it is used for. In the inventory, the furnace and chests, point at an item and press {key.handbook} or click the small ? on it.
chapter.qtcraft.basics.handbook.title: This handbook
chapter.qtcraft.building.parts.text: Many materials come as stairs, slabs, walls, fences and gates. Fences, walls and panes connect to their neighbours. Doors, trapdoors and gates open and close when used; sneak to place a block against them instead.
chapter.qtcraft.building.parts.title: Building parts
chapter.qtcraft.building.placing.text: Use the held block on a face (right mouse button) to place it next to that face. Stairs and furnaces turn by your view, slabs and stairs go high or low by where you click, torches and ladders hang on the face you click. Tall grass is replaced by what you place into it.
chapter.qtcraft.building.placing.title: Placing blocks
chapter.qtcraft.building.support.text: Torches, ladders, lamps, doors and plants need something to stand or hang on. When it goes, they break and drop. Sand and gravel fall when nothing is below them.
chapter.qtcraft.building.support.title: Support
chapter.qtcraft.controls.keys.text:
- **Mouse**: look around (click into the window first), or **{key.lookUp} {key.lookLeft} {key.lookDown} {key.lookRight}**
- **{key.forward} {key.left} {key.back} {key.right}**: walk, **{key.jump}**: jump or swim up, **{key.sneak}**: sneak, **{key1.sprint}**: sprint
- **Left mouse** or **{key.mine}**: mine, attack a creature
- **Right mouse** or **{key.use}**: place, use, eat
- **Middle mouse** or **{key1.pickBlock}**: pick the block you look at
- **{key.drop}**: throw one item, **{key.stackModifier}+{key1.drop}**: the whole stack
- **{key.hotbar1}–{key.hotbar9}**, mouse wheel: choose the hotbar slot
- **{key.inventory}**: inventory, **{key.chat}**: chat, **{key.command}**: command, **{key.cameraView}**: camera view, **{key.handbook}**: handbook, **{key.debugOverlay}**: debug display (off, compact, full), **{key.debugOptions}**: debug options, **{key.pause}**: menu
- Every key except Esc can be changed under Settings → Controls.
chapter.qtcraft.controls.keys.title: Keys and mouse
chapter.qtcraft.controls.mac.text: On a Mac the keys F1–F12 control the brightness, Mission Control, the search and other system features, so the game does not receive them. Every action therefore has a letter key, for example **{key1.cameraView}** for the camera view and **{key1.handbook}** for the handbook pages. To use the function keys in the game, hold fn or switch on “Use F1, F2, etc. keys as standard function keys” in the system settings (Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Function Keys). No key of the game uses Cmd, and keys pressed with Cmd do nothing in the game, because macOS keeps Cmd+Q, Cmd+H, Cmd+W, Cmd+Space and Cmd+Tab for itself: sprint is Option on a Mac, and Control+{key1.drop} throws the whole stack. If you put an action on Control, note that Control with the arrow keys or Space switches desktops or the input source. Option+E, U, N and I are dead keys only while typing text; in the world they work as sprint plus that key.
chapter.qtcraft.controls.mac.title: Mac keyboards
chapter.qtcraft.controls.moving.text: You walk at {player.walkSpeed} m/s, sprint at {player.sprintSpeed} m/s and sneak at {player.sneakSpeed} m/s; sneaking keeps you from falling off edges. To sprint, press **{key1.sprint}** while walking forward or tap **{key.forward}** twice; the sprint lasts as long as you keep walking forward. The view widens a little while you sprint (Settings → FOV effects). Steps up to {player.stepHeight} m are climbed without jumping. In water you swim at {player.swimSpeed} m/s.
chapter.qtcraft.controls.moving.title: Moving
chapter.qtcraft.controls.screens.text: In the inventory, furnace and chest screens a left click picks a stack up and puts it down (merging or swapping), a right click puts down a single item. The list on the right of the inventory crafts recipes directly.
chapter.qtcraft.controls.screens.title: Screens
chapter.qtcraft.crafting.book.text: The inventory lists what you can make right now; a click crafts it. Some recipes ask for a group such as any planks or coal or charcoal: every item of the group fits.
chapter.qtcraft.crafting.book.title: Recipe list and groups
chapter.qtcraft.crafting.grid.text: The inventory has a 2 × 2 grid; a crafting table within {crafting.tableReach} m opens 3 × 3. Lay out the ingredients as the recipe shows (shaped recipes may sit anywhere in the grid and be mirrored, shapeless ones in any order) and take the result. Leaving the screen puts the grid back into the inventory.
chapter.qtcraft.crafting.grid.title: The crafting grid
chapter.qtcraft.creatures.limits.text: Near each player there are at most {mobs.hostileCap} hostile, {mobs.passiveCap} peaceful and {mobs.ambientCap} ambient creatures. Hostile and ambient creatures farther than {mobs.despawnDistance} m from every player vanish. Peaceful animals stay: about one in ten new chunks brings a group of them, they wait while their area is not loaded and are saved with the world. New ones only appear near you while no animal is around.
chapter.qtcraft.creatures.limits.title: Limits
chapter.qtcraft.creatures.spawning.text: Creatures appear {mobs.spawnRadiusMin}–{mobs.spawnRadiusMax} m away from players: peaceful animals on grass by day, hostile ones in the dark at night and in caves at least {mobs.caveDepth} blocks below the surface. Torches and lamps keep hostile creatures away. Each page lists the blocks, biomes, time and light a creature needs.
chapter.qtcraft.creatures.spawning.title: Where creatures appear
chapter.qtcraft.death.death.text: At zero health you die. Respawn takes you back to the spawn point with full health and food. With the game rule keepInventory (on by default) you keep your items; otherwise they scatter where you died.
chapter.qtcraft.death.death.title: When you die
chapter.qtcraft.death.items.text: Items on the ground vanish after {items.despawnSeconds} s while their area is loaded. Items you throw can be picked up again after {items.thrownPickupDelay} s.
chapter.qtcraft.death.items.title: Dropped items
chapter.qtcraft.health.fighting.text: Left-click a creature within {player.attackReach} m to hit it, at most every {player.attackCooldown} s. Swords and axes deal more damage than the hand; every hit knocks the target back.
chapter.qtcraft.health.fighting.title: Fighting
chapter.qtcraft.health.health.text: You have {player.maxHealth} health points, shown as hearts. Falls deeper than {player.fallDamageThreshold} m cost one point per further metre; landing in water or on a ladder is safe. Hostile creatures, lava and starving hurt as well. After a hit you cannot be hurt for {player.hurtInvulnerability} s.
chapter.qtcraft.health.health.title: Health
chapter.qtcraft.hunger.effects.text: With at least {hunger.regenerationFood} food points you heal one health point every {hunger.regenerationInterval} s. With an empty food bar you lose one health point every {hunger.starvationInterval} s, but hunger alone never takes you below {hunger.starvationFloor}.
chapter.qtcraft.hunger.effects.title: Healing and starving
chapter.qtcraft.hunger.food.text: The food bar holds {hunger.maxFood} points. Hold food and use it (right mouse button) to eat when you are not full. Walking, sprinting, swimming, jumping, mining, fighting and being hurt make you hungry: every {hunger.exhaustionPerFood} points of exhaustion cost one food point. Walking empties a full bar in about {hunger.walkMinutesForFullBar} min, sprinting in about {hunger.sprintMinutesForFullBar} min; jumps, mining and fights cost a little extra. Healing one health point costs {hunger.regenerationFoodPerHealth} food points.
chapter.qtcraft.hunger.food.title: Eating
chapter.qtcraft.mining.breaking.text: Hold the left mouse button on a block within {player.reach} m. Each hardness point takes {mining.secondsPerHardness} s by hand; the right tool divides that time by its speed. Broken blocks drop their items, which you pick up by walking over them.
chapter.qtcraft.mining.breaking.title: Breaking blocks
chapter.qtcraft.mining.tools.text: Stone and ores need a pickaxe of a certain level: wood is level {qtcraft:wooden_pickaxe.toolLevel}, stone {qtcraft:stone_pickaxe.toolLevel}, iron {qtcraft:iron_pickaxe.toolLevel}, diamond {qtcraft:diamond_pickaxe.toolLevel}. With a weaker tool or none, mining takes {mining.secondsPerHardnessWithoutTool} s per hardness point and drops nothing. Tools wear out with every block.
chapter.qtcraft.mining.tools.title: Tools and levels
chapter.qtcraft.rules.rules.text: **keepInventory**: keep the inventory on death (chosen when creating a world). **daylightCycle**: the time of day runs. **mobSpawning**: creatures appear by themselves. Show a rule with `/gamerule <rule>`; operators change it with `/gamerule <rule> true|false`. The chapter Commands lists every command.
chapter.qtcraft.rules.rules.title: Game rules
chapter.qtcraft.commands.basics.text: Open the chat with T (or /) and type a command starting with `/`. `/help` lists the commands you may use, `/help <command>` shows how to use one. `~` stands for your position in coordinates (`~2` is two blocks further). A server without a window (`qtcraft-headless --console`) reads the same commands from its console, there without the leading `/`; every command is written to the server log with who ran it.
chapter.qtcraft.commands.basics.title: Using commands
chapter.qtcraft.commands.cheats.text:
- `/give <item> [count]`, `/spawnitem <item> [count]`
- `/summon <creature> [count]` (at most {commands.summonLimit} creatures), `/kill`, `/heal`, `/feed [points]`
- `/equip <set|armour|clear>` puts on armour (`/equip iron`)
- `/summon armor_stand [property=value …]` and `/armorstand <nearest|looking|id> <property> [values]` place and change armour stands. Properties: `pose <head|body|left_arm|right_arm|left_leg|right_leg> <x> <y> <z>` (degrees), `rotation <degrees>`, `arms`, `plate`, `small`, `showname` with `true|false`, `name [text]`, `equip <set|item>`, `cape <cape|none>`, `clear`, `reset`; `info` lists them. Stand ids are only valid until the world is loaded again; scripts use `nearest` or `looking`. In `/summon` values follow `=` separated by commas: `/summon armor_stand equip=iron pose=right_arm,90,0,0 small`.
chapter.qtcraft.commands.cheats.title: Items, creatures and armour
chapter.qtcraft.commands.control.text:
- `/time [set day|night|<seconds>]`, `/time add <seconds>`
- `/gamerule <keepInventory|daylightCycle|mobSpawning> [true|false]`
- `/gamemode [survival|creative] [player]`: shows or changes the game mode, `/defaultgamemode [mode]`: the mode of new players
- `/tick freeze` and `/tick unfreeze`: the world stands still (time of day, creatures, liquids, plants, machines, hunger), players keep moving; `/tick step [ticks]` moves a frozen world on
- `/tick rate <1..100>` or `/tick rate reset` (20 per second): how fast the world runs
- `/tick sprint <ticks|seconds s|minutes min|hours h|days d>`: run that much game time as fast as possible (`/tick sprint stop` ends it)
- `/tick query`: rate, measured rate, freezing and the time per tick phase
Rate and freezing are not saved; a world always opens normally.
chapter.qtcraft.commands.control.title: Time and ticks
chapter.qtcraft.commands.macros.text: Mods add commands as macros (`commands/*.json`): a name and command lines that run one after another with your rights, so a macro never lets you do more than you may do anyway. `/help` lists them with the others.
chapter.qtcraft.commands.macros.title: Commands from mods
chapter.qtcraft.commands.players.text:
- `/list`: who is online
- `/locatebiome <biome>`: where the nearest place of a biome is
- `/kick <player> [reason]`: disconnect a player (he may come back)
- `/ban <player> [reason]`, `/unban <player>`, `/banlist`: keep a name out of this world
- `/whitelist on|off|list|add <player>|remove <player>`: with the whitelist on, only listed players and operators join; a ban holds for operators too
- `/op [player]`, `/deop <player>`: operator rights; `/op` alone lists the operators
- `/tp <x> <y> <z>`, `/tp <player>`, `/tp <player> <x> <y> <z>`, `/tp <player> <target player>`: teleport
Operators, bans and the whitelist are saved with the world. The host of a world cannot be kicked, banned or lose his rights.
chapter.qtcraft.commands.players.title: Players
chapter.qtcraft.commands.repair.text:
- `/regenerate [<x> <z> [<x2> <z2>]]`: generate the chunk at your feet (or the chunks of an area, at most {commands.maxRegenerate}) again as the world type makes it; every change in it is lost, chests and furnaces in it lose their contents
- `/remove <mobs|hostile|animals|ambient|items|stands|all|<creature>|item:<item>> [radius|world]`: remove entities within 32 m (at most {commands.maxRemoveRadius} m) or in the whole loaded world; `all` means creatures and items
- `/fill <x1> <y1> <z1> <x2> <y2> <z2> <block> [replace <block>]` and `/clear <x1> <y1> <z1> <x2> <y2> <z2> [block]`: fill a box or turn it into air, at most {commands.maxFill} blocks; `replace` and the block of `/clear` limit the change to one kind of block
- `/setblock <x> <y> <z> <block>`
- `/save`: save now; `/backup [label]`: save and copy the world folder into the folder backups next to the worlds, named with date and time
- `/worldinfo`: loaded chunks, entities, tick times and memory
chapter.qtcraft.commands.repair.title: Repairing and cleaning up
chapter.qtcraft.commands.rights.text: Most commands are for **operators**. In single player you are always an operator; on a server, operators make others operators with `/op <player>` and take the rights away with `/deop`. Every player may use `/help`, `/list`, `/locatebiome`, reading a game rule, `/confirm` and `/cancel`. Commands that destroy a lot wait for `/confirm` (within {commands.confirmSeconds} s; `/cancel` drops them): `/regenerate`, `/fill` and `/clear` of more than {commands.confirmFill} blocks, `/remove` of more than {commands.confirmRemove} entities, of armour stands or in the whole world.
chapter.qtcraft.commands.rights.title: Operators and confirmations
chapter.qtcraft.multiplayer.joining.text: Choose **Multiplayer** in the main menu, type the server's address and your player name and click **Join**. An address is `host`, `host:port`, `192.168.1.20:25601` or `[IPv6 address]:port`; without a port the game uses 25600. Give the password only if the server has one. While the game connects and logs in you can cancel; if the server refuses you, the screen says why (wrong password, full server, other mods, a name that belongs to someone else, a ban). Servers you joined appear under **Recent servers**: a click puts the address into the field, **Join** joins at once, **×** removes the entry. Passwords are never saved.
chapter.qtcraft.multiplayer.hosting.titl: Opening your world to the LAN
chapter.qtcraft.multiplayer.hosting.text: In a single-player world, open the menu (Esc) and choose **Open to LAN**. Pick a port (0 takes any free one), an optional password and how many players may join, then **Open to other players**. The screen shows the port and the addresses of your computer; friends in the same network join with one of them. You keep playing as before and stay the world's operator; **Stop hosting** or leaving the world closes it again. The firewall may ask once whether QtCraft may accept incoming connections.
chapter.qtcraft.multiplayer.server.title: Dedicated server and the internet
chapter.qtcraft.multiplayer.server.text: A server without a window runs with `qtcraft-headless --server`; its settings (name, message of the day, port, password, player limit, world, view distance, operators) are in `server.json` in its data folder, written at the first start. Players over the internet need the server's port forwarded in the router to the server computer, or a server with a public address; QtCraft uses no relay servers.
chapter.qtcraft.multiplayer.players.text: Hold **{key1.playerList}** to see who is online: the server's name and message of the day, every player with operators marked and your own name highlighted. The chat tells when somebody joins or leaves. If the connection ends, the game says why; **Join again** connects to the same server, **Back to menu** leaves. In the menu (Esc) of a network game, **Disconnect** leaves the server; the server keeps your inventory and position.
chapter.qtcraft.multiplayer.safety.title: Limits of the security
chapter.qtcraft.multiplayer.safety.text: There are no accounts: every installation has a random key that proves your name on each server (the first player to use a name on a server keeps it). Passwords are never sent in plain text, but nothing else is encrypted, so chat and play can be read on the way. Open a server to the internet only with a password and to people you know.
chapter.qtcraft.smelting.furnace.text: A furnace takes something to smelt on top and fuel below; the result appears on the right. It burns one fuel item at a time while it has work, and keeps working while you are away as long as its area is loaded. Breaking it drops what is inside.
chapter.qtcraft.smelting.furnace.title: Smelting
chapter.qtcraft.world.liquids.text: Water and lava flow from their sources; a bucket takes a source and pours it elsewhere. Where lava meets water it hardens into obsidian or cobblestone. Lava lights its surroundings, burns items and hurts.
chapter.qtcraft.world.liquids.title: Water and lava
chapter.qtcraft.world.time.text: A full day lasts {day.length} s. The world is generated from its seed while you explore it; only what you change is saved.
chapter.qtcraft.world.time.title: Day and night

handbook.slot.head: Head
handbook.table.armourText: Armour is worn in four slots next to the character in the inventory: drag it there, shift-click it or right-click with it in the hand. Every armour point takes 4 % off the blows of creatures and the burns of lava and magma, up to 20 points (80 %); falls and hunger go through. Each such hit wears every worn piece by a quarter of the damage (at least 1); a piece breaks when its durability is used up. Two worn pieces of the same kind in the crafting grid make one with both durabilities plus 5 %.
mob.qtcraft.caped_mannequin.description: A mannequin wearing the green cape. It walks about slowly, so the cape swings; it never appears by itself, the showcase world has one at the character stand.
chapter.qtcraft.creative.modes.title: Survival and creative
chapter.qtcraft.creative.modes.text: Every player has a game mode. In **survival** you gather, craft, eat and can die. In **creative** you build freely: every block and item without limit, flying, blocks break at the first strike, nothing hurts you and you never get hungry. A new world asks for the mode of its players in the main menu (**Game mode**); operators change it with `/gamemode creative` or `/gamemode survival` (also for another player: `/gamemode creative Alice`), and `/defaultgamemode` sets the mode of players who join for the first time.
chapter.qtcraft.creative.flying.title: Flying
chapter.qtcraft.creative.flying.text: Tap **{key.jump}** twice quickly to take off or to stop flying. While flying, **{key.jump}** rises, **{key.sneak}** sinks and **{key1.sprint}** doubles the speed ({player.flySpeed} m/s, sprinting {player.flySprintSpeed} m/s); the view widens a little. Sinking onto the ground lands you and ends the flight. The showcase world has a platform high above the ground that only flyers reach.
chapter.qtcraft.creative.inventory.title: Creative inventory
chapter.qtcraft.creative.inventory.text: **{key.inventory}** opens the creative inventory: every block and item of the game and of the loaded mods, sorted into tabs (blocks, building parts, tools and armour, food, other items) with a search that finds names in your language, English names and ids like `oak_planks`. A left click takes a full stack, a right click one item, a shift-click puts a full stack straight into the inventory; click a slot to put it there. The bin deletes a stack. **Crafting and armour** leads to the usual inventory with the crafting grid and the armour slots.
chapter.qtcraft.creative.rules.title: Rules in creative mode
chapter.qtcraft.creative.rules.text:
- Blocks break at once (even bedrock) and drop nothing; chests and furnaces still lose their contents.
- Placing a block keeps your stack, a poured bucket stays full.
- No damage except `/kill`; creatures leave you alone; food stays as it is.
- **Middle mouse** or **{key1.pickBlock}** puts the block you look at into your hand; in survival this selects it when it is in your inventory.
chapter.qtcraft.creative.switching.title: Changing between the modes
chapter.qtcraft.creative.switching.text: Survival and creative each have their own inventory and armour. Changing the mode puts the current ones aside and brings back those of the other mode, so creative items never end up in your survival inventory. Health and food stay as they were. Chests belong to the world: what you put into a chest in creative mode is there in survival too.
